theme_central: The golden ornaments of this world (zukhruf) measure nothing of one's worth before Allah — true wealth is divine mercy, not gold.
sources_note: Structure in 7 rukus / 9 thematic paragraphs sourced (dorar.net, thelastdialogue.org). Detail of boundaries reconstructed from known landmarks (Ibrahim 26-35, Musa/Pharaoh 46-56, Aissa as a sign of the Hour 57-65).

branches.title: Opening
branches.resume: Revelation in clear Arabic, the Mother of the Book with Allah.

children.t: Revelation in clear Arabic, exalted in the Mother of the Book

branches.title: Contradictory recognition
branches.resume: They recognize Allah as creator yet associate deities with Him; blessings of transport, on land and sea.

children.t: Contradictory recognition of Allah as creator; blessings of transport

branches.title: Daughters attributed to Allah, blind conformism
branches.resume: Refutation of attributing daughters to Allah; criticism of "we found our fathers upon a religion".

children.t: Refutation of attributing daughters to Allah (the angels)
Criticism of blind conformism to the ancestors

branches.title: Ibrahim, wealth and worth
branches.resume: Ibrahim rejects his father's religion; material wealth does not make a man's worth.

children.t: Ibrahim rejects his father's religion, a word that remains among his descendants
Material wealth does not measure worth before Allah

branches.title: The demon companion, regret
branches.resume: Whoever turns a blind eye to the Reminder is assigned a demon companion; bitter regret on the Day of Judgment.

children.t: Demon companion assigned to those blind to the Reminder, regret at the Judgment

branches.title: Musa/Pharaoh, Aissa a sign of the Hour
branches.resume: Musa sent to Pharaoh with clear signs, drowning; Aissa given as an example, a sign heralding the Hour.

children.t: Musa sent to Pharaoh, mockery, drowning
Aissa given as an example, sign heralding the Hour, divergence of the sects

branches.title: Paradise, Hell, closing
branches.resume: Friends turned enemies except the pious, fate of the criminals, final refutation of a son attributed to Allah.

children.t: Friends turned enemies that Day except the pious, description of Paradise
Fate of the criminals in Hell, calling out to the guardian Malik
Final refutation of a son attributed to Allah, the Prophet's patience
